title: We put the creativity, AI puts the work, but for a game to become successful it needs one thing more: The business side of it
author: Codingology
selftext:
Hi! I watched this [yt video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2r2FsyPCObI) talking about some things around game development that are not often discussed about.  
The creator rightfully says that people focus too much on 2 things: The ideas and the realizations. However there is a third step that he comments on, that is needed in order for a game to become great, which is the more entrepreneur side of it.  
Finding clients, marketing on socials, commercialization (the process of transforming a product into a business) and similar activities.

Are you focusing on those?  
I noticed that I keep on having great ideas for my game, and I find new ways to make claude more efficient at realizing those; however, no one knows my game exists yet.  
And for now I'm okay with this to be honest. With all the stories we've been hearing about scummy AI devs that replicate your game on roblox before yours even gets out, I prefer to keep the secret as long as possible.   
But still; I never thought once about the marketing side. I can't even begin to think what kind of videos / post I should make online. 

Are you guys worrying about this side of the project?   
And if yes, are you using AI even on this parameter or all the marketing ideas are your own?  
How much do you think we should focus on the business side of the projects, now that AI has removed a huge part of labor?

comments.author: TheLastTuatara
comments.body:
God damn does anyone write their own posts anymore. 

“Finding clients” - really? Gamers are clients now? Lol

replies.author: Agile_Branch_8743
replies.body: If you’re building games professionally, yes.

comments.author: mentiondesk
comments.body: Getting your game noticed is just as important as building it, and sharing your journey online early can help build an audience and get feedback. If you're unsure where to start with marketing and community engagement, there are tools like ParseStream that track relevant discussions and alert you about potential leads, so you can join conversations at the right time without feeling spammy.

comments.author: blackskies69
comments.body:
Absolutely not. My dream is to raise the quality of AI slop to such a degree that corporate media has no choice but to submit to my sloppiness. I'll release my games open sourced and free to play so others can enjoy it, learn from it, and my work to make their own cool shit I get to play some day. I get infinite games and AAA gaming companies hopefully fuck off forever. Getting it noticed sure thats something I think about, but I'm not going to worry about money. In my opinion games are the least cool thing we could make with AI, but it's the best thing we can make with it at the moment. 

Any who, free info dump:

Do you want multiplayer for your game but don't know networking or don't want to pay hosting fees? Use a virtual LAN to connect up to 10 players to a single lobby. If you want to get spicy with it use an amazon ec2 instance (you get a 6 month one for free), and set it up as a linux machine then have claude set up veth connections between two virtual LAN's to pair lobbies. Now you can have infinite lobbies that players can hop between. All for free.

replies.body: I agree! I currently finally finished a project have a small community! And some grinders asking me what’s next ?!? Like chill!

comments.body: Element 3 is simply a matter of element 2 + element 1 plus time.  It's possible to fake it with substantial skill and effort, but it's both difficult and a poor longterm investment.
